title: Historian's toolkit card: the six concepts
subject: History
source: Seeded from history/y7 lesson 5 (Historian's toolkit card: the six concepts (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 5: Historians, Christendom and the Islamic world in 1095. To understand how historians think and what Christendom and the Islamic world were like in 1095

questions.q: Which historical concept is about the order of events?
questions.model: Read the toolkit. Order of events = chronology. So the answer is chronology.

questions.q: Why did the Byzantine emperor need help in 1095?
questions.a: The Seljuk Turks had taken much of his land after Manzikert in 1071

questions.q: Why is Jerusalem holy to Muslims?
questions.a: Al-Aqsa Mosque is there; it was the first qiblah and linked to the Night Journey

questions.q: Core: Label the map: Rome, Constantinople, Baghdad, Cairo, Jerusalem; shade Christendom and the Islamic world.
questions.a: Correctly placed cities; Western and Byzantine Christendom shaded; Seljuk and Fatimid lands shaded
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: Constantinople on the strait between Europe and Asia; label it 'Byzantine capital'.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, write a paragraph describing the Islamic world in 1095. Start: 'In 1095 the Islamic world was ...'
questions.a: For example: rich in learning and trade but divided between the Abbasids, the Seljuks and the Fatimids

questions.q: Stretch: Why might divisions in the Islamic world matter if an army attacked?
questions.a: Divided rulers might not unite to defend their lands

questions.q: Jerusalem had been under Muslim rule since:
Big question: what did the world around Jerusalem look like in 1095?
questions.a: Christendom split between the Pope's West and the Byzantine East; the Islamic world rich but divided between Seljuks and Fatimids; Jerusalem holy to all three faiths
